name: RV-8803 real-time clock breakout
description: Micro Crystal RV-8803-C7 temperature-compensated real-time clock (32.768 kHz crystal inside, +/-1.5 ppm from 0 to 50 C, factory calibrated): hundredths of seconds, seconds to years in BCD with leap years 2000-2099, 24-hour only, alarm, countdown timer, periodic update interrupt, time-stamped external event input and clock output, on a 400 kHz I2C bus at fixed address 0x32. Chip runs on 1.5-5.5 V and draws about 240 nA timekeeping. Sold as: SparkFun Real Time Clock Module - RV-8803 (Qwiic), BOB-16281, 8-pin header GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL, EVI, INT, CLKOUT, CLKOE plus two Qwiic connectors, 4.7 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups (I2C jumper), 100 kOhm pull-ups on EVI and INT, 100 kOhm pull-down on CLKOE, and a CR1225 backup cell diode-ORed with 3V3.
eli5: A very accurate clock that remembers the date and time, kept running by a little coin cell while your board is off.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (feeds the chip through a BAS70 diode, and the on-board SDA/SCL/INT/EVI pull-ups)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, open-drain; 4.7 kOhm pull-up to 3V3 on the board (cut the I2C jumper to remove)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, up to 400 kHz; 4.7 kOhm pull-up to 3V3 on the board

pins.name: EVI
pins.description: External event input with time stamp (active LOW by default), 100 kOhm pull-up and push button on the board; not needed for basic use

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output (alarm/timer/update/event), open-drain, active LOW, 100 kOhm pull-up on the board; not needed for basic use

pins.name: CLKOUT
pins.description: Clock output (32.768 kHz, 1024 Hz or 1 Hz), push-pull, only active while CLKOE is high; not needed for basic use

pins.name: CLKOE
pins.description: Clock output enable, 100 kOhm pull-down on the board (CLKOUT off); drive high to enable CLKOUT; not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: SparkFun Real Time Clock Module RV-8803 Qwiic BOB-16281
buildNotes: Fixed I2C address 0x32; only one RV-8803 per bus.

Power the 3V3 pin from 3.3 V: the board's 4.7 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups go to this pin. The chip itself sits behind a BAS70-05 diode that also lets the CR1225 cell take over automatically when 3V3 is removed (no setting needed).

Time registers 00h-06h: seconds, minutes, hours (always 24 h), weekday, date, month, year. Burst-read them; the chip cannot freeze its counters, so if seconds read 59 the driver reads again and keeps the second burst if it changed (App. Manual 4.12).
Set the time with the RESET bit (control 0Fh bit 0) held at 1, then release it: the clock starts exactly at the seconds written (App. Manual 4.13).
The weekday register is one-hot (one bit per day, meaning chosen by you). The driver writes bit n = weekday n with 0 = Sunday, and returns the weekday worked out from the date.
V2F/V1F (flags 0Eh bits 1:0) are set at power-on: the time is invalid until set. The driver clears them when you set the time.
Leave EVI and CLKOE unconnected for basic use; the board's pull-up/pull-down keep them in a safe state.

driver.code:
# RV-8803-C7 temperature-compensated real-time clock (Micro Crystal), MicroPython driver.
# I2C address 0x32. Registers per the Micro Crystal RV-8803-C7 Application Manual (Rev. 1.7):
# 00h-06h seconds, minutes, hours (always 24 h), weekday (one bit per day), date, month, year (BCD,
# address auto-increments; mirrored at 11h-17h), 10h hundredths of seconds (read only),
# 08h-0Ah alarm (bit 7 AE = 1 disables that field), 0Dh extension (WADA bit 6, TEST bit 7 must stay 0),
# 0Eh flags (AF bit 3, V2F bit 1, V1F bit 0), 0Fh control (AIE bit 3, RESET bit 0).
_ADDR = 0x32
_SECONDS = 0x00
_HUNDREDTHS = 0x10
_ALARM_MIN = 0x08
_EXT = 0x0D
_FLAGS = 0x0E
_CTRL = 0x0F

_WADA = 0x40
_AF = 0x08
_V2F = 0x02
_V1F = 0x01
_AIE = 0x08
_RESET = 0x01


def _bcd(n):
    return ((n // 10) << 4) | (n % 10)


def _dec(b):
    return (b >> 4) * 10 + (b & 0x0F)


def _weekday(y, m, d):
    # 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday (Sakamoto's method).
    t = (0, 3, 2, 5, 0, 3, 5, 1, 4, 6, 2, 4)
    if m < 3:
        y -= 1
    return (y + y // 4 - y // 100 + y // 400 + t[m - 1] + d) % 7


class RV8803:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=_ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _r(self, reg, n=1):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _w(self, reg, data):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes(data))

    def _read_time(self):
        # The RV-8803 cannot freeze its counters during a read (App. Manual 4.12). If the seconds read
        # 59, read again: if they changed, the first burst may be half-incremented, so use the second.
        r = self._r(_SECONDS, 7)
        if (r[0] & 0x7F) == 0x59:
            r2 = self._r(_SECONDS, 7)
            if (r2[0] & 0x7F) != 0x59:
                r = r2
        return r

    def datetime(self, dt=None):
        """Read or set the time (24-hour, years 2000-2099).
        Read returns (year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second), weekday 0 = Sunday,
        worked out from the date. Set with (year, month, day, hour, minute, second)."""
        if dt is None:
            r = self._read_time()
            y, mo, d = 2000 + _dec(r[6]), _dec(r[5] & 0x1F), _dec(r[4] & 0x3F)
            return (y, mo, d, _weekday(y, mo, d), _dec(r[2] & 0x3F), _dec(r[1] & 0x7F), _dec(r[0] & 0x7F))
        y, mo, d, h, mi, s = dt[:6]
        if not 2000 <= y <= 2099:
            raise ValueError('year must be 2000-2099')
        # App. Manual 4.13: RESET = 1 holds the prescaler (and clears the hundredths), write the
        # time, then RESET = 0 starts the clock exactly at the seconds written.
        c = self._r(_CTRL)[0] & 0x3D
        self._w(_CTRL, [c | _RESET])
        try:
            # Weekday register: exactly one bit set, bit n = weekday n (0 = Sunday).
            self._w(_SECONDS, [_bcd(s), _bcd(mi), _bcd(h), 1 << _weekday(y, mo, d),
                               _bcd(d), _bcd(mo), _bcd(y - 2000)])
        finally:
            self._w(_CTRL, [c & ~_RESET])
        f = self._r(_FLAGS)[0]
        self._w(_FLAGS, [f & 0x3C])  # clear V2F and V1F (POR / low-voltage flags): time is now valid

    def hundredths(self):
        """Hundredths of a second, 0-99."""
        return _dec(self._r(_HUNDREDTHS)[0])

    def lost_power(self):
        """True if V2F is set: power-on reset or the supply fell below VLOW2 (about 1.2 V),
        so the time is invalid until set."""
        return bool(self._r(_FLAGS)[0] & _V2F)

    def set_alarm(self, minute=None, hour=None, date=None, interrupt=True):
        """Alarm on the fields given (None = ignore that field; hour 0-23, date 1-31).
        AF is set on a match; the open-drain INT pin goes low if interrupt is True."""
        c = self._r(_CTRL)[0] & 0x3D
        self._w(_CTRL, [c & ~_AIE])  # AIE = 0 while changing the alarm
        f = self._r(_FLAGS)[0]
        self._w(_FLAGS, [f & ~_AF & 0x3F])  # AF = 0
        e = self._r(_EXT)[0] & 0x7F  # TEST must be written 0
        self._w(_EXT, [e | _WADA])  # WADA = 1: 0Ah is a date alarm
        g = lambda v: 0x80 if v is None else _bcd(v)
        self._w(_ALARM_MIN, [g(minute), g(hour), g(date)])
        if interrupt:
            self._w(_CTRL, [c | _AIE])

    def alarm_fired(self):
        return bool(self._r(_FLAGS)[0] & _AF)

    def clear_alarm(self):
        """Clear AF (INT is released); the alarm stays armed."""
        f = self._r(_FLAGS)[0]
        self._w(_FLAGS, [f & ~_AF & 0x3F])

    def disable_alarm(self):
        c = self._r(_CTRL)[0] & 0x3D
        self._w(_CTRL, [c & ~_AIE])
        self._w(_ALARM_MIN, [0x80, 0x80, 0x80])
        self.clear_alarm()

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from rv8803 import RV8803

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
rtc = RV8803(i2c)
rtc.datetime((2029, 12, 31, 23, 59, 57))  # Monday 31 Dec 2029, 23:59:57
while True:
    y, mo, d, wd, h, mi, s = rtc.datetime()
    print('wd=%d %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d' % (wd, y, mo, d, h, mi, s))
    time.sleep(1)
